meta.title: Thai Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 415 expressions · 48 everyday, 340 idioms, 27 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 415 Thai set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 48 everyday phrases, 340 idioms and 27 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Thai A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — the everyday formulas a Thai speaker uses as one piece (เจอกัน, กี่โมง, สบายดีไหม …), greetings for the day and the festivals, and the words on signs. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (ตกหลุมรัก, รับฟัง, หนอนหนังสือ …) — Thai is rich in them, many built from four words in two rhyming pairs — and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (ฟังหูไว้หู, กองทัพเดินด้วยท้อง, กำขี้ดีกว่ากำตด …). Thai writes no spaces between words, so an expression here is a headword that divides into two or more dictionary words. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Thai sentences contain them; Tatoeba's Thai is small, so only 18 of the 415 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of their count in the Thai National Corpus and the Thai Textbook Corpus. Every expression is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the tone of every syllable. Real example sentences come with 84 of the 415 expressions, three apiece for 33, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, romanisation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then the word counts of the Thai National Corpus and the Thai Textbook Corpus as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR, and Wiktionary.
